Subject: Private deployment: ownership matrix for network interfaces & CI safety net

Team / Atlas,

Following our pre-kickoff, attaching an initial ownership matrix and a short sketch of CI gates for the Atlas Health private deployment. The three vectors I want us to align on before the architecture review: 1) module ownership (Terraform layer), 2) runtime config (Helm + annotations for the eBPF LB), 3) post-deploy operations (Ansible roles / runbooks).

High-level asks:
- Please mark column ownership in ownership_matrix_v1.xlsx (Terraform / Helm / Ansible / Ops).
- Marcus: can you call out clear boundaries for network interfaces — specifically where SR-IOV and VLAN config live (tf module vs. ansible)?
- Soojin: propose CI gating (smoke/connectivity/perf) and rollback triggers we can bake into the pipeline.
- Atlas (Toria): confirm air-gapped image flow and encryption/KMS expectations so we can pin secret-handling responsibilities.

Attachments: ownership_matrix_v1.xlsx, proposed-ci-gates.md. Drive link included: https://drive.redwood.com/privdeploy/atlas/ownership_matrix_v1

Goal: 30-minute alignment sync tomorrow (2026-10-01). If you can’t make it, please add comments to the spreadsheet and I’ll capture outstanding action items.

Thanks,
Camila
Camila Reyes
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment: ownership matrix for network interfaces & CI safety net

Thanks Camila — quick read and first pass notes inline.

Key callouts:
- Network interface boundaries: prefer to separate L2/vlan provisioning (Terraform: networking module) from SR-IOV device plugin setup and firmware tuning (Ansible: host prep). The terraform module should declare logical interfaces and attachable SR-IOV capacity as resources, not attempt NIC firmware changes.
- Firewall & network policies: put high-level security group and NSX load into Terraform, but concrete iptables/ebtables rules that are host-local belong with Ansible.
- Helm values: we should expose an annotation set for the eBPF LB so the infra team can toggle connection tracking and tc settings without Helm chart patching. That avoids chart churn.

I attached a minimal terraform sketch (network-interface-draft.tf) with module boundaries. Will drop a draft change to the ownership sheet.

Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Infra Eng, Redwood

Hi Camila and team,

Thanks — this looks good as a starting point. A few items from Atlas side:
- Air-gapped images: we need a documented flow for image ingestion into our private registry (checksums, signed manifests). Who owns the signed-image handoff?
- KMS & secrets: our security team requires that secret creation is triggered from our KMS (HSM-backed). Is Redwood planning to call our KMS or will you provide encrypted bundles for us to unwrap on-prem?
- Audit retention: procurement needs a statement that audit logs (auth events + API request logs) can be retained for 7 years. We’ll need the specific S3/object-store locations and retention controls documented.
- Rollback acceptance: would like to see the acceptance tests that must pass before we flip traffic back — who on Redwood owns the rollback playbook?

We’ll review the attachments and add comments in the sheet. For the sync: 10/01 10:00am ET works for us.

Thanks all — short CI/CD proposal below (will add to proposed-ci-gates.md):

Pipeline stages (suggested):
1) lint/plan: terraform plan (module-level), helm lint + chart-schema validation. Block on plan diffs that affect networking modules without explicit owner sign-off.
2) image-scan & signature check: ensure images are signed; for air-gapped flows allow a manual ingestion step with artifact fingerprints.
3) infra-smoke: apply to staging namespace + basic connectivity tests (pod-to-pod, pod-to-storage, LB reachability).
4) perf-sanity: short RPS test at 5% of expected production to verify tail latency; fail if p99 outlier > threshold.
5) rollout-canary: incrementally route traffic (10% -> 30% -> 100%) with automated rollback if connectivity or error-rate thresholds breached.

Rollback triggers and owners:
- Immediate auto-rollback if LB health checks fail > 2x within 5 minutes (Ops-owned).
- Manual rollback if audit/retention or KMS issues detected (Security/Redwood Solutions to coordinate).
- Ansible-runbook will include a host-level revert path (package rollback + NIC driver downgrade) — Ops to update.

I’ll take the primary action on CI gating implementation and the smoke test harness. Marcus — please sign off on the SR-IOV boundary in the sheet so I can reference the owner in the pipeline blocks.

Thanks,
Soojin
Senior SRE, Redwood
